_comment: Operator-owned reference data for the deterministic phishing analyzer
(soc_copilot/phishing.py). Three lists, each deliberately curated rather
- brands: the brand tokens worth impersonating, mapped to the
organizational domains ACTUALLY authorized to send as them. A brand
token appearing in a display name or a subdomain is only a signal when
the sending organizational domain is not on this list. Inferring brand
ownership from the name alone is how a tool starts flagging
- url_shorteners: hosts whose whole purpose is to hide the destination.
A WEAK signal on its own (marketing and internal comms use them too);
it means 'the destination was not inspectable', not 'malicious'.
- free_mail: consumer mail providers. A Reply-To here on a message whose
From is a corporate or brand domain is the canonical BEC/invoice-fraud
Add to brands only domains the brand genuinely sends from, including its
outsourced senders — a missing entry produces a false positive on
legitimate mail, which is the failure mode that gets a detection muted.
